Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 8e25a0e266b05f414a63bf04b30d9a7e085e94fc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Archit Taneja <architt@codeaurora.org>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2017 16:29:04 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm/dsi: Fix bug in dsi_mgr_phy_enable

A recent commit introduces a bug in dsi_mgr_phy_enable. In the non
dual DSI mode, we reset the mdsi (master DSI) PHY. This isn't right
since master and slave DSI exist only in dual DSI mode. For the normal
mode of operation, we should simply reset the PHY of the DSI device
(i.e. msm_dsi) corresponding to the current bridge.

Usage of the wrong DSI pointer also resulted in a static checker
warning. That too is resolved with this fix.

Fixes: b62aa70a98c5 (drm/msm/dsi: Move PHY operations out of host)

Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Archit Taneja <architt@codeaurora.org>
Reviewed-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@gmail.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_manager.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_manager.c
index 921270ea6059..a879ffa534b4 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_manager.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_manager.c
@@ -171,7 +171,7 @@ dsi_mgr_phy_enable(int id,
 			}
 		}
 	} else {
-		msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(mdsi->host);
+		msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(msm_dsi->host);
 		ret = enable_phy(msm_dsi, src_pll_id, &shared_timings[id]);
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dsi/dsi_manager.c`**
   - **Line Change**: The line that previously called `msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(mdsi->host);` has been modified to `msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(msm_dsi->host);`.
   - **Purpose**: This change corrects the usage of the DSI pointer. Instead of resetting the PHY of the master DSI (which is only relevant in dual DSI mode), it now resets the PHY of the DSI device corresponding to the current bridge, which is appropriate for non-dual DSI mode.

### Relationships

- The modification in `dsi_manager.c` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified as `b62aa70a98c5`) that incorrectly handled the PHY reset in non-dual DSI mode. The change resolves a static checker warning related to the incorrect DSI pointer usage, ensuring that the code functions correctly in both single and dual DSI configurations. The patch is a direct response to the issues reported by Dan Carpenter and has been reviewed and signed off by Rob Clark.

2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
struct msm_dsi *mdsi = dsi_mgr_get_dsi(DSI_CLOCK_MASTER);
msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(mdsi->host);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because in non-dual DSI mode, the code incorrectly resets the PHY of the master DSI (`mdsi`) instead of the current DSI device (`msm_dsi`). This leads to improper behavior since master and slave DSI should only be referenced in dual DSI mode.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
msm_dsi_host_reset_phy(msm_dsi->host);
ret = enable_phy(msm_dsi, src_pll_id, &shared_timings[id]);
```
Reason:
The fix changes the reset operation to correctly reference the current DSI device (`msm_dsi`) instead of the master DSI (`mdsi`). This ensures that the PHY reset and enable operations are performed on the appropriate DSI device, resolving the bug and the static checker warning.
